**Finding: compliant** (rule LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer)

The document imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum termination fee on IBM, so it sits at the **preferred** position — no redline proposed.

What I checked and why it clears:

- **No LD language at all** — a full-text search for "liquidated" returns zero hits.
- **The only "penalty" runs against MSL** (§7.3 b), p0757): a responsiveness shortfall triggers a percentage penalty on MSL's Work Center material cost, "invoiced by IBM to MSL." Per the detection guidance, vendor-payable amounts are compliant and in our favour.
- **Delinquency / Shipment Profit Rate tables** (§7.2, sec-p0752) and **§10.4 Delays in Shipment** (MSL bears premium air-freight costs for late shipment) likewise operate as credits or cost-shifts against MSL.
- **Termination and PO cancellation carry no exit fee.** §6.1 lets IBM cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time, with no cancellation charge where MSL is in default; convenience cancellation only preserves cost reimbursements under the Price section. §§5.2–5.3 confine IBM to paying for completed/partially completed Product and Parts actually procured against IBM forecasts (capped so IBM never pays more for partial than completed Product) — that is cost recovery, not a stipulated sum.
- **Inventory/flexibility exposure is contained.** §13.2 e) states IBM "will have no liability for unused flexibility," and §13.3 b) leaves EOL inventory not transferred to IBM as "the sole responsibility of MSL."
- **§9.0 Premium Cost** is reimbursement of MSL's actual materials/labour cost, gated by IBM pre-approval above a threshold and limited to genuinely unplanned demand beyond Supply Flexibility — a cost pass-through, not a penalty.

Noted but not flagged: the several "IBM shall pay MSL [*]" line items (§16.21, Attachment 4 expense participation, amendments) are fixed expense-participation and startup subsidies, not damages triggered by IBM breach or termination, so they fall outside this rule.
